Final for Publication

"NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
2150 WEST CHICAGO AVENUE, CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated along the Chicago Avenue Bus
Corridor. The zoning lot is currently vacant. The Applicant intends to redevelop this property
with a new 4-story residential building with 3 dwelling units and 3 parking spaces located in the
garage, with rooftop decks to be located on the principal building and the garage. The Applicant
needs a zoning change to a B2-2 District to allow residential use on the ground floor at the
property, with optional variation and administrative adjustment relief for an increase of up to 10%
in the height of the proposed building, reduction in the rear setback, and to allow parking ratio in
excess of 0.5 parking space per unit.

Project Zoning Change from a B3-2 Community Shopping District to a B2-2
Description: Neighborhood Mixed-Use District.

Use: Residential Building with 3 Dwelling Units and 3 parking spaces.
Lot Area: 25; x 123.05’ = 3,076.25 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 2.08

Floor Area: 6,404 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 1,025 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking spaces: 3 (see administrative adjustment request below)
Parking:

Setbacks: Front: 1’

Side: 3’ on the west side and 1’ on the east side
Rear: 2’ (see variation request below)

Building Height: | 49°-6” per the attached plans (see variation request below)


Final for Publication

1 The applicant will comply with Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served

Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In B and C districts, any new
construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the

following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served

Locations:
The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is located along the Chicago Bus Corridor.

It is not located within the prescribed distance from any CTA or META station so Section 17-3-
0308 is not applicable to this redevelopment.

2. The project is not required to comply with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504,
since it is not located along a pedestrian street and is designated in a non-commercial use group,
pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets. Even though the subject property is
not located along Pedestrian Street or Pedestrian Retail Street, the project still complies with the

following criteria:

(a) The entire building fagade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The requirements of Section 17-3-0504-C Transparency standards do not apply to the subject
development as proposed building is entirely residential (non-commercial use group) and there is
no commercial space which would require clear, non-reflective windows, and the project will not

provide any product display windows.
(c) The building will have a primary entrance door facing Chicago Avenue.

(d) Alll off-street parking spaces will be located in the garage and will not be visible from the
right-of-way.

(e) Vehicle access to the parking area will come via the alley, per site plan attached.

3. The project is not required to comply with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly
Development Guide: Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or
guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan Commission. This Criteria is not applicable to this

project.

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the
Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0207 with
any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces
are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE:

The Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is in excess of 50% of the Minimum Automobile
Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0207, so in case this Section is
determined to be applicable to this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is requesting an
Administrative Adjustment via Optional Relief (see below) to increase the parking from 2 spaces
required to 3 parking spaces proposed (1:1 ratio).

Final for Publication

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to issue
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this section. This Criteria is not
applicable to this project.

Il. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) With this Type 1 Rezoning, the Applicant also seeks relief for Administrative Adjustment
under section 17-13-1003-EE, from the parking requirements of Section 17-3-0308(4) to
increase the on-site parking requirements from 2 parking spaces required to 3 parking
spaces proposed.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-3-0405-A, which states that for floors containing
dwelling units, the minimum rear setback is 30 feet. While the building is setback 40’, the
garage is setback 2’ from the rear property line, as required. Since the rear staircase for the
building also will provide access to the garage roof top deck, the Applicant needs the rear
setback variation from 30” to 2”.

(C) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under Section 17-13-1101-A and Section 17-
13-1003-L Building Height, to allow an increase of up to 10% in the height of a building,
from the height requirements of Section 17-3-0408-A, to increase the maximum height of
45 feet permitted to 49.5 feet proposed, per the attached plans.

(D) | The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the
proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
create practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject property has a
substandard depth. The property has been vacant for many years and needs this relief to stimulate
its redevelopment.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible with
the existing land use pattern on the subject block, which is improved with multi-story and multi-
unit, mid-density residential buildings. Furthermore, the new dwelling units will increase the
variety of available housing stock, in response to the growing housing demand in the
neighborhood.
